coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic character directly named and described in the selected Level 1 official synopsis: Will, Blood, Mary, and Gus. Peoples, undead as a category, vocational labels, gods, magic, places, reincarnation, moral language, and story systems remain terms rather than character nodes.
omissions: All other named figures, later-volume developments, exact prose/chapter wording, prior-life identity, magic mechanics, divine identities, locations beyond the unnamed city description, and outcomes are omitted because they are not established by this metadata witness.
The web novel, manga, anime, games, Japanese Overlap Bunko edition, guidebooks, and any other adaptations or editions are separate witnesses.
The publisher's fictional good/bad-gods phrasing is not a statement about real religions; no real-world religious taxonomy is mapped from it.
Death, grief, violence, and content details beyond the dead-city/undead premise and J-Novel Club's suggested 15+ audience are not expanded without inspected prose.
uncertainties: The official page lists a reincarnation tag, but its synopsis does not establish Will's former identity, memories, mechanism of rebirth, or the setting's full isekai system; none is asserted here.
No browser-readable page or chapter locator was available for the selected English prose, so claims are limited to the publisher synopsis and credits.
The staff announcement says the series is based on a hit web novel but does not demonstrate wording or continuity equivalence between that web novel and this light-novel edition.
The series page bears an anime tag, but no anime content, characterization, or adaptation claim is used.
evidence_basis: J-Novel Club first-party English Level 1 metadata and a staff announcement only; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, adaptation recap, uninspected prose, or illustration is used.
